title: Language Transformers and Meaning · Level 2
slo: Explain how a language transformer represents relationships among words.

options.rationale: An embedding is a vector. It represents semantic attributes of a token or visual patch.
A word or phrase is a token. An embedding is the vector representation of semantic attributes.

feedback.intrinsic: The item is confused with its representation.
feedback.instructional: An embedding is a semantic vector.

options.rationale: Attention weighs relationships among tokens in context. An embedding is a vector, not the weighting mechanism.
options.better_fit: This describes attention in a transformer.

feedback.intrinsic: The model mechanism would be mislabeled.
feedback.instructional: Embeddings are vectors; attention relates tokens.

options.text: A portion of an image containing pixels
options.rationale: An image patch is a portion of pixel values. Although a patch can receive an embedding, it is not itself the embedding.
options.better_fit: This describes an image patch for a vision transformer.

feedback.intrinsic: Visual input would be confused with its numeric representation.
feedback.instructional: An embedding represents a token or patch as a vector.

exercises.explanation: Correct. An embedding is a semantic vector.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The model's purpose is not expressed clearly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Connect the model to embedding relationships and token similarities.

exercises.correct_answer: A semantic language model uses embedding relationships to represent language-token similarities.
exercises.explanation: Embedding relationships represent similarities among language tokens.

exercises.question_text: The technique that uses relationships among tokens in context is called ___.

parts.text: The technique that uses relationships among tokens in context is called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The response names an input or representation instead of the technique.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use attention for contextual token relationships.

exercises.explanation: Attention models contextual relationships among tokens.

exercises.question_text: A company must analyze comments, translate them, and draft replies. Which capabilities should it select from a semantic language model? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Analyzing comments is a text-analysis task. Semantic language models support this NLP capability.
Translating comments is a language task. Semantic language models can support translation.
Drafting replies requires generating language. This is a supported NLP task.
Object locations concern objects in images. The scenario requires processing and producing written language.
options.better_fit: Use object-location prediction to locate products in photos.

feedback.intrinsic: The comments and replies would not be handled.
feedback.instructional: Choose text analysis, translation, and language generation.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Each selected capability addresses a language need in the scenario.

parts.text: Transformer encoders create vectors with many

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The response names an input or mechanism rather than a vector property.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use dimensions for the coordinates of a high-dimensional vector.

exercises.explanation: Transformer encoder embeddings are high-dimensional vectors.

exercises.question_text: A message contains the word “bank,” and nearby words must determine whether it means a river edge or a financial institution. Which technique should the engineer use?

options.rationale: Attention uses relationships among nearby tokens. It allows the context to shape the representation of “bank.”
An image patch is a pixel-based visual input. It cannot use nearby words to resolve word meaning.
options.better_fit: Use patches to process a camera image.

feedback.intrinsic: The ambiguity in the message remains unresolved.
feedback.instructional: Use attention to relate “bank” to its surrounding words.

options.rationale: A fixed definition ignores the surrounding words that disambiguate “bank.” The scenario requires a context-sensitive representation.
options.better_fit: A fixed definition may work for a term with only one intended meaning.

options.rationale: A pixel-label classifier assigns classes to image pixels. It does not analyze relationships among words in a message.
options.better_fit: Use pixel classification for semantic segmentation of images.

feedback.intrinsic: The text would not receive contextual analysis.
feedback.instructional: This is a language-context decision, so choose attention.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Attention resolves meaning through surrounding-token context.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the statement into the correct order.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the model, then the token, embedding, and numeric form.

exercises.correct_answer: A model represents a token with an embedding as numeric values.
exercises.explanation: A model represents a token using an embedding made of numeric values.

exercises.question_text: Put the vision-transformer process in order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The conversion step lacks its required input.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Extract image patches before converting them into vectors.

exercises.correct_answer: Train on images extract image patches convert patches into linear vectors
exercises.explanation: A ViT is trained on images, extracts patches, and converts patches into linear vectors.

exercises.question_text: A catalog system maps written product names to numeric meaning representations. Which terms should its designer use? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Each written product name is language input and can be treated as a token. Tokens are the units being represented.
An embedding is a vector representing semantic attributes. It can represent the product-name token numerically.
The numeric representation is an ordered array of values. That array is a vector.
An image patch contains pixel values from a visual input. The scenario provides written names rather than product photos.
options.better_fit: Use image patches when processing product photographs with a ViT.

feedback.intrinsic: Written names would be treated as image data.
feedback.instructional: Use tokens and embeddings for written language.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The design maps a language token to an embedding vector.

exercises.question_text: A neural-network architecture that uses embeddings and attention to model language context is a ___.

parts.text: A neural-network architecture that uses embeddings and attention to model language context is a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The response names a different concept.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The architecture is called a transformer.

exercises.explanation: A transformer uses embeddings and attention to model contextual relationships.

exercises.question_text: A smart checkout must analyze product photos with a vision transformer. Which actions should its engineer include? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A ViT extracts image patches, which are portions of pixel values. Product photos therefore provide appropriate patch-based input.
A ViT converts image patches into linear vectors. These vectors allow the transformer approach to process visual data.

options.text: Use image data as the model input.
options.rationale: The scenario is based on product photos. Vision transformers are designed to apply transformer processing to image data.

options.text: Represent each photo as a language token.
options.rationale: Language tokens represent written input rather than the pixel structure of photos. A ViT needs image patches for product photos.
options.better_fit: Use language tokens for written product descriptions.

feedback.intrinsic: The photos would lose their pixel-based structure.
feedback.instructional: Use image patches and vectors for visual inputs.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The selected actions follow the ViT image-patch approach.

exercises.question_text: A support team must analyze how words relate within customer messages. Which architecture should it choose?

options.rationale: The input is written language. A language transformer models contextual relationships among tokens.
A vision transformer processes image patches. Customer messages are language, not image regions.
options.better_fit: Use a vision transformer to analyze product photographs.

feedback.intrinsic: The messages would not be represented as language.
feedback.instructional: Choose a language transformer for token relationships.

options.rationale: Pixel segmentation assigns labels to image pixels. It does not model relationships among words in messages.
options.better_fit: Use segmentation when each pixel in an image needs a class label.

feedback.intrinsic: The text-analysis goal would remain unmet.
feedback.instructional: This task requires a language architecture.

options.rationale: Image-patch extraction divides visual input into pixel regions. It provides no language-token context for customer messages.
options.better_fit: Use patch extraction as part of a vision transformer pipeline.

feedback.intrinsic: Words would have no contextual representation.
feedback.instructional: Language messages should be handled as tokens by a transformer.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The decision is driven by the language input and contextual-word task.
